title: Relative flat extension from a prescribed flat cone replacement
statement: Let E,H be cochain complexes of module sheaves on a small ringed site, and f:E -> H. Assume E has bounded-above flat terms, and prescribe a bounded-above flat complex Q with a quasi-isomorphism r:Q -> Cone(f). There exist a bounded-above flat complex F, maps t:E -> F and g:F -> H, such that g is a quasi-isomorphism and t followed by g equals f strictly. No epimorphy for g is asserted. [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]

proof.text: Write the components of r as a^i:Q^i → E^{i+1} and b^i:Q^i → H^i using mappingCone.fst and mappingCone.snd. The chain map identity for r gives a^i d_E + d_Q a^{i+1}=0 and d_Q b^{i+1}=a^i f^{i+1}+b^i d_H. Construct F with F^i=E^i ⊞ Q^i and differential matrix ((d_E,-a),(0,d_Q)). The first identity proves the differential squares to zero. The inclusion t of E and the map g=(f,b) are chain maps, and t followed by g equals f strictly by the biproduct identities.

Choose the maximum of the given bounds for E and Q. Above it both summands are zero, so F is zero. Apply finite coproduct flatness to the ULift WalkingPair family of the two terms, and transport its exact tensor functor along the canonical isomorphism of that coproduct with the binary biproduct. Thus every F^i is flat.

The summands of Cone(g)^i are E^{i+1}, Q^{i+1}, H^i, whereas Cone(r)^i has summands Q^{i+1}, E^{i+1}, H^i. Define a degreewise isomorphism permuting the first two summands. Verify its inverse using the cone inclusions and projections. Check differential compatibility by projecting to the three summands: the Q coordinate uses d_F followed by snd = snd followed by d_Q; the E coordinate uses d_F followed by fst = fst followed by d_E minus snd followed by a; the H coordinate uses g=(f,b). These are the defining matrix identities.

Apply the cone acyclicity criterion [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] to r and g. The hypothesis hr makes Cone(r) acyclic. The explicit complex isomorphism transfers vanishing of its homology to Cone(g); the criterion then gives QuasiIso g. This is the existing sorry-free source-library theorem, used as a tool, not a different unit route.

mathlib_searches.query: relative cone replacement; adding contractible flat disks for termwise epimorphic augmentation

mathlib_searches.results: mappingCone, fst, snd, inl, inr, descCochain, liftCochain and isZero_X_iff; tools for construction, no relative flat extension or flat disk augmentation theorem.

No matching flat relative extension or flat epicification theorem. Mathlib CM5a/CM5b use injectives and lower bounds; unsuitable. Project bounded flat replacements are the existing source of the cone replacement.

lean.statement: theorem exists_relative_boundedAbove_flat_extension (E H : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ) (f : E ⟶ H) (hE : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (E.X i)) (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (E.X i)) (Q : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ) (r : Q ⟶ mappingCone f) (hQ : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (Q.X i)) (hflatQ : ∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (Q.X i)) (hr : QuasiIso r) : ∃ (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ) (t : E ⟶ F) (g : F ⟶ H), (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (F.X i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (F.X i)) ∧ QuasiIso g ∧ t ≫ g = f
